title: The command line reads the product's configuration
description: `lathe check` calls `loadWorkspace` on the product root, which reads `lathe.config.json`: the specs folder, the meta-model extensions, the product's checks folder and `structure.maxChildren`.

title: The loader finds and parses every record file
description: Every `*.md` file under the specs folder but a README is read and its header parsed. A file that cannot be parsed becomes a `parse-error` problem, and the rest still load.

title: The loader merges the meta-model and loads the records into DuckDB
description: Lathe's `kinds.csv`, `relations.csv`, `sections.csv` and `ids.csv` are merged with the product's extensions, and the records, fields, links and file facts are loaded into tables of an in-memory database.
statements: one CREATE TABLE per table, then its rows

title: The loader writes the settings the checks read
description: The `settings` table gets one row per setting a check reads, such as `structure.maxChildren`.

title: Lathe's checks run in file order, then the product's own
description: Each check file is one SELECT over the same tables, returning `(severity, check, record, message)` rows; each is named by its file name.

title: Coverage is counted per domain and obligation kind
description: Designed, built, proved and planned are counted for every obligation kind in every domain, with the gaps.
statements: the coverage counts, gaps and tests-by-state queries

title: The command prints the report and sets the exit status
description: Errors are printed first, then warnings, then a coverage line per domain and obligation kind; the exit status is 1 when there is an error.

title: With --json, the command prints the whole workspace instead
description: After the same load, `--json` prints the `Workspace` as JSON in place of the text report.
